headline: Georgia Students Cut School Cafeteria Food Waste by 70%
meta_description: Elementary school students discovered their cafeteria was wasting 450 pounds of food daily. Six years later, they had slashed waste by 70% and redistributed ov…
summary_short: Students at a Georgia elementary school tackled a problem nobody was talking about: their cafeteria threw away 450 pounds of food every single day.
body:
Students at a Georgia elementary school discovered their cafeteria was wasting nearly 450 pounds of food each day—a staggering amount that might have gone unnoticed without their curiosity and determination to act.

What began as an observation turned into real change. Over six years, the students implemented solutions that cut waste by 70%, a dramatic reduction that transformed how their school approached food. Beyond simply preventing waste, they took the extra step of redistributing more than 20,000 food items annually, ensuring that surplus meals reached people who needed them.

The project reveals how young people can identify systemic problems in their own communities and drive meaningful solutions. By paying attention to what was happening in their cafeteria, these students didn't just improve their school—they created a model for reducing food waste while fighting hunger.
